gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured input latency for any keyboard in these combos. The only lab figure I could open is Gamepadla's 21.51 ms average over the dongle (22.47 ms over Bluetooth) for Logitech's MX Keys S, which is not mechanical. I could not open a single named measurement for any mechanical keyboard or mouse ChatGPT showed.
standout_why: I opened four rival pages on 2026-11-10. keyboardverdict.com (rank 1) says 'we don't test products ourselves', and its only figures are maker specs such as the RedThunder K10's 3,800 mAh battery and the MX Master 3S's 8,000 DPI. reviewed.com (rank 3) gives only typing results ('over 80 wpm' on the MK270/MK320) and no latency, noise or measured battery. mechkeyfoundry.com (rank 5) quotes only Logitech claims (MX Master 3S 70 days, MX Mechanical Mini 15 days with backlight) and says the author took no measurements. gamingreviewguide.com (rank 6) says it uses 'manufacturer specifications ... rather than in-house testing'. deskfinds.com (rank 4) returned 403. So every rival has zero lab numbers, which makes a measurement new. But the one figure I could open is for the MX Keys S, a combo that keyboardverdict and mechkeyfoundry already flag as 'mechanical feel', not mechanical. That makes it useful context rather than a fact that decides the pick.
decides: It doesn't change the pick. The Gamepadla figure only gives a reference point for Logitech's non-mechanical office combo: about 21.5 ms average with roughly 6 ms jitter over either the dongle or Bluetooth. That fits an office board and is not a gaming result. A latency comparison that would decide between the gaming combos (HyperX Alloy Origins Core + Pulsefire Haste vs the Redragon S136/S168 vs the MSI Forge GK320) or confirm the MX Mechanical as the office pick needs RTINGS or TechPowerUp. Neither could be opened in this run, so this angle should not anchor the page unless those pages are fetched in another way.

findings.label: Keyboard input latency, USB receiver (Gamepadla test #6387)
findings.value: 9.92 ms min / 21.51 ms avg / 33.09 ms max, 5.94 ms jitter
findings.note: Tested 2025-08-30 by John Punch using the Prometheus 82 method: physical actuation with a contact sensor as the timing reference, measured until the PC software registers the input. Windows 11 build 10.0.26100, program v5.3.2.0, DInput. Scissor-switch board, not mechanical; kept as the reference for Logitech's 'mechanical feel' combo that rival pages list.
